description: Enforceable absolute-claims register. bannedTerms: categorical / quasi-legal wording banned from public copy — an absolute 'non-partisan' self-label, 'anonymous', 'unlinkable', an absolute legal-compliance claim, 'no personal information', 'cannot recognise/track', 'IP addresses are never collected' — each with the softer wording to prefer. permittedClaims: the narrow exceptions, each a specific claim at a specific location allowed by a CURRENT control-register evidence record, carrying the qualification that makes it defensible (permitted_qualification + mustContain), the unqualified wording it may never regress to (prohibited_absolute_wording), an evidence_owner and a review_date/expiry_date. Enforced fail-closed by scripts/check-absolute-claims.mjs (Legal CI group). See docs/claims-register.md for the wider claim↔substantiation map.

bannedTerms.label: an absolute 'non-partisan' self-label
bannedTerms.prefer: independent / independently developed using a published methodology

bannedTerms.label: an absolute 'anonymous' claim
bannedTerms.prefer: de-identified / no direct identifiers are stored in the research database

bannedTerms.label: an absolute 'unlinkable' claim
bannedTerms.prefer: sent as a separate request / designed to reduce linkability

bannedTerms.label: an absolute legal-compliance claim
bannedTerms.pattern: \blegally compliant\b|\bfully compliant\b|\bguaranteed compliant\b|\blegally the sole\b|\bsole authoriser\b
bannedTerms.prefer: describe the specific control, not a blanket compliance or sole-authoriser guarantee

bannedTerms.label: an absolute 'cannot recognise/track' claim
bannedTerms.prefer: is not designed to recognise or track you

bannedTerms.label: an absolute 'IP address is never collected' claim
bannedTerms.prefer: no IP address is stored in the research database

permittedClaims.claim: The privacy policy describes the research group counts as 'not personal information' to support indefinite retention.
permittedClaims.permitted_qualification: Scoped to genuinely aggregated group totals with no per-person record; the aggregates are still reviewed after each federal election and the operative protection is the disclosure controls (k-suppression), stated on the same page — not an absolute deletion or non-identifiability promise.
permittedClaims.prohibited_absolute_wording: your data is anonymous and can never identify you

permittedClaims.claim: The privacy policy states the analytics collects no personal information.
permittedClaims.permitted_qualification: Tied to the cookieless, edge-only construction of Cloudflare Web Analytics (sets no cookie, stores nothing on the device, assigns no identifier); the claim follows from that design and is scoped to this provider, not a product-wide assertion.
permittedClaims.prohibited_absolute_wording: we never collect any information about you

permittedClaims.claim: The privacy policy states the analytics cannot be used to recognise or track people across visits or sites.
permittedClaims.permitted_qualification: Follows directly from the cookieless, identifier-free construction (no cookie, no device identifier); scoped to this analytics provider, not a global tracking-impossibility claim.
permittedClaims.prohibited_absolute_wording: we can never track anyone anywhere

permittedClaims.claim: The methodology page states the research holds no name, contact detail, IP address or device identifier.
permittedClaims.permitted_qualification: Backed by the transmitted-field allowlist that never sends the IP, and immediately qualified on the same page — a small-count residual re-identification risk is acknowledged, not an absolute non-identifiability guarantee.
permittedClaims.prohibited_absolute_wording: you are completely anonymous and cannot ever be identified
mustContain: no technique eliminates every possible risk

permittedClaims.claim: The third-party services registry states no personal data is involved in / disclosed to the public parliamentary-data source.
permittedClaims.permitted_qualification: Factual statement about one specific data flow — the retrieved content is public parliamentary voting records — not a blanket product-wide 'no personal information' claim.
permittedClaims.prohibited_absolute_wording: How2Vote holds no personal information about anyone
